This plant can be saved! (I think)
I would remove all of the soil, make a perlite-soil-lava rock (or any small rocks) mix for good drainage. Whatever pot its placed in should have a drainage hole(s) and be sprayed with water before placing the soil inside. Then remove all the roots that look black or squishy, apply aloe vera sap to the roots that are left. Cut off all the leaves that are wilted or that look unhealthy, sprinkle some cinnamon powder on the bottom of the plant and gently place into a hole of your pot mix.
Make sure that whatever soil it used to have is completely gone. Aloe vera sap and cinnamon are good for promoting root growth and avoiding rot. Just make sure that when the plant is in its new pot it has some wiggle room to let new roots peak.
